newsitem.title: GERMANY: German feeds plant says customers ignore soy row.
newsitem.headline: German feeds plant says customers ignore soy row.

text.p: The German Raiffeisen feeds plant targeted by environmental group Greenpeace in a protest over the use of transgenic soymeal said its consumers had no problems with the new commodity.
"The discussion has not been relevant to farmers over the last weeks and months," said a spokesman at the 500,000 tonnes-a-year feeds plant operated by Raiffeisen-Central-Genossenschaft (RCG).
"We can't guarantee products free of transgenic soymeal, which Greenpeace demands, but nobody in the market can give such guarantees."
Greenpeace has not mentioned potential cost savings from the new products that will eventually mean lower costs to the farmer," he said.
The row is over meal derived from imported United States soybeans genetically modified by Monsanto Co, which is cleared for use here but Greenpeace thinks may hold risks.

In Bonn, a spokesman for the umbrella organisation of Raiffeisen plants (DRV), which group Germany's farm co-operatives, said DRV was operating in accordance with the law and raw materials input was completely transparent.
"If farmers insist they want protein sources other than soya in their feeds mix, we can offer such products," he said.
"But farmers are led by prices and no such separate demand is apparent."
DRV accounts for 40-50 percent of total German compound feed output and marketing of 20 million tonnes a year.
Greenpeace last month staged protests at tow other Raiffeisen plants in Schleswig-Holstein state and Bavaria.
